`GET /invoices/<id>` now returns a 404 when the invoice doesn't exist, instead of crashing. I couldn't test it: Flask isn't installed in this environment, so my quick check failed on the import before it reached the route.

The change in `src/api/invoices.py`:

```python
invoice = _INVOICES.get(invoice_id)
if invoice is None:
    return problem(404, "Invoice not found", f"No invoice with id {invoice_id!r}.")
```

Before this, a missing id made `.get()` return `None`, and the next line, `invoice.__dict__`, raised an error that came back as a 500.

A project memory says API errors must use the standard error format, built with `problem()` from `src/api/errors.py`, so I used that rather than an ad-hoc dict. The response body looks like `{"type": "about:blank", "title": "Invoice not found", "status": 404, "detail": "..."}`.

I didn't add a test because `tests/` has none for the invoices API yet. I can add one if you'd like.
